research.summary: Personal cash pays for roles; the game rewards useful team services. Separate player transfers, shared FOB supplies and permanent access from per-life kit spending.
research.scope: Read from Spend Time and Spend Money through access, resource commitment, contribution, settlement and player outcomes. Real money never directly buys account cash. Start here, then open WARDOGS — mechanics and cash settlement in the library for all 26 mechanisms. Launch announcements checked 14 September 2026; August frames are explicitly older. Exact death/refund and player-payment settlement remain open.
limitations: No unsupported 90% refund formula is used.
Beta screenshot prices are not launch prices.
Black Market, Vault, gold conversion and reset details are announced systems, not verified live mechanics.
Player transfer amounts and system rewards must be accounted separately.

interpretations.note: Economic implications and discussion prompts are analysis. Edges show causal or resource relationships, not measured numerical conversion rates.

Input and outcome framing is economic analysis. Access is required for participation; it is not a real-money purchase of the opening cash grant. All feedback pipes are labeled and distinct from the forward reading order.

details.explanation: One spendable account balance funds kits, access and useful team roles. The official description grants $10,000 at the start of the player journey and says cash survives matches.
details.implications: Account cash is the stock. Match profit is a change in that stock, not another wallet. Cash is not all erased because an attempt ends.
details.prompt: Can a nearly broke player still afford an effective support role?

details.explanation: Vendor purchases exchange personal cash for equipment. Guns, magazines, ammunition and utility choices must be budgeted together. Older inspected screens show access locks separately from cart purchases.
details.implications: Paying for the kit and subsequently losing it must not be recorded as two cash debits. Equipment loss creates the need for a future replacement purchase.
details.prompt: Which part of the ordinary kit is reusable value and which is consumable?
uncertainties: Current item-by-item refund rules remain unverified.

details.explanation: Death ends the active attempt and leads back to equipment decisions. Public guides contradict each other about a 90% refund: death versus surviving to match end. Neither formula is accepted here without a continuous cash ledger. Inspected August footage shows downed state, a respawn countdown and a return to base with a rifle. Its intervening balance change is not itemised, so it cannot establish the cause or refund rate.
details.implications: The measured cost of another attempt is the next actual purchase, adjusted by any verified refunds. Treating total account cash as lost would also be wrong.
details.prompt: What changes on the account balance immediately after give-up, before re-buy?
uncertainties: Exact death refund, surviving-kit refund, dropped gear ownership and quit settlement require current continuous footage.

details.explanation: The same account balance carries into another match. The accounting identity includes system rewards, incoming player payments, purchases, outgoing payments and any actual settlement adjustments. There is no assumed extraction checkpoint.
details.implications: Sustainable equipment choices depend on ordinary net earnings across many lives. A profitable session can subsidize an expensive experimental role later.
details.prompt: How many routine support runs finance one high-risk vehicle attempt?

details.explanation: The developer explicitly names reviving as a cash-rewarded contribution. The rescuer commits time and medical capability; the teammate returns to action.
details.implications: The reward subsidizes a service with benefits beyond the rescuer. Rescue can also preserve position and avoid another deployment journey.
details.prompt: Is the ordinary reward enough without a bribe?
details.reviewFingerprint: {"label":"Restore a teammate","kind":"action","sources":["System cash reward"],"sinks":["Medical supplies / risk"],"values":["Teammate resumes play"],"notes":"Game pays for a revive; no fixed payout asserted.","edges":[{"from":"kit","to":"revive","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"Choose a medical support role"},{"from":"revive","to":"carry","type":"cross-lane","feedback":false,"label":"System revive reward"}]}

details.explanation: Current official description promises double cash in the moving Hot Zone. The developer mode explanation separately doubles contribution to team presence. Majority presence earns team points toward the match win.
details.implications: The moving premium tries to align personal earnings with the team objective. Cash and team score are different ledgers; a bonus to one must not be inferred for every other action.
details.prompt: Does the premium compensate for the extra exposure?
uncertainties: Exact event eligibility, payout ticks and stacking formulas are not established.
details.reviewFingerprint: {"label":"Hold the Control / Hot Zone","kind":"action","sources":["Objective cash"],"sinks":["Time and exposure"],"values":["Team presence"],"notes":"Hot Zone: double cash; developer also states double presence.","edges":[{"from":"kit","to":"zone","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"Equipment enables objective play"},{"from":"zone","to":"carry","type":"cross-lane","feedback":false,"label":"System cash rewards"}]}

details.explanation: The official store explicitly rewards transporting friendlies to the Control Zone. Older gameplay demonstrates passenger transport and logistics delivery.
details.implications: The game purchases a public service from a player: transport capacity benefits teammates who did not buy the vehicle.
details.prompt: What prevents profitable transport routes from becoming unhelpful shuttling?
details.reviewFingerprint: {"label":"Deliver teammates","kind":"action","sources":["Transport reward"],"sinks":["Vehicle / pilot risk"],"values":["Teammates at the objective"],"notes":"System rewards delivery; passengers are not assumed to pay a fare.","edges":[{"from":"cash","to":"transport","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"Fund a vehicle and transport role"},{"from":"transport","to":"carry","type":"cross-lane","feedback":false,"label":"System transport reward"}]}

details.explanation: A seller buys a crate and its stock, sets a markup and deploys a field shop. A teammate purchase moves cash from buyer to seller and stock in the opposite direction. The detailed map separates stocking from sale.
details.implications: Cash changes hands; any separately paid XP or game subsidy needs a separate entry. The launch adjustment is evidence that rewarding transaction count can invite low-value farming.
details.prompt: Does seller markup compensate useful logistics without pricing teammates out?
uncertainties: Direct two-account sale settlement and any fee are not inspected.

details.explanation: Private cash buys FOB infrastructure, tools and physical supply pallets. Delivery converts those pallets into shared Build, Ammo, Fuel and Mechanical resources. The detailed map separates purchase, delivery and consumption.
details.implications: Separate resource bottlenecks create interdependence: cash alone cannot erect a structure at an empty FOB. Supply allocation affects everyone using the base.
details.prompt: Can a builder deplete shared stocks faster than the team replenishes them?
uncertainties: Exact live build recipes, structure rewards and repair consumption need inspected launch UI.

details.explanation: Developer material describes multiple progression tracks. Launch notes distinguish Career and role gates and rebalance the XP curve away from weekend-beta pacing.
details.implications: A player can have cash without the required access, or access without enough cash. These are separate constraints on role choice.
details.prompt: Does slow access progression delay learning the role?
details.reviewFingerprint: {"label":"Earn Career and role XP","kind":"action","sources":["Career / role XP"],"sinks":[],"values":["Progression thresholds"],"notes":"XP is earned progress, not spendable cash.","edges":[{"from":"kit","to":"xp","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"Eligible play earns progress"},{"from":"xp","to":"unlock","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"XP meets the access gate"}]}

details.explanation: The Season 1 notes put Large Hammer at Support level 8 and list its Support access payment separately from its vendor price. Inspected older unlock-confirmation UI corroborates that access is purchased before an item instance.
details.implications: The $75,000 is an investment in eligibility; treating it as every-use cost would overstate the role’s running expense. Unlocks are not a free issued kit.
details.prompt: How quickly does a useful role make its access investment feel worthwhile?
uncertainties: No claim that access survives an announced future season reset.
details.reviewFingerprint: {"label":"Pay for purchase eligibility","kind":"action","sources":[],"sinks":["Access-unlock cash"],"values":["Persistent purchase access"],"notes":"Large Hammer: Support 8; $75,000 access; $2,400 vendor.","edges":[{"from":"cash","to":"unlock","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"In-game cash pays access charge"},{"from":"unlock","to":"kit","type":"value","feedback":true,"label":"Unlocked purchase eligibility; not an item"},{"from":"xp","to":"unlock","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"XP meets the access gate"}]}

details.explanation: The published Early Access policy sells game access with optional Supporter cosmetic content and rejects selling in-game cash or gold. This is a commercial payment outside the match cash loop.
details.implications: Revenue is separated from players’ equipment liquidity. Earned progression remains a design and retention lever without selling replacement cash.
details.prompt: Can the commercial model sustain the expected support cadence?
details.reviewFingerprint: {"label":"Buy game access / Supporter extras","kind":"action","sources":[],"sinks":["Real money"],"values":["Access / cosmetic entitlements"],"notes":"Developer policy: no paid cash or gold.","edges":[{"from":"commerce","to":"identity","type":"final","feedback":false,"label":"Access to optional cosmetics"},{"from":"commerce","to":"kit","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"Game access required; no currency sale"},{"from":"money","to":"commerce","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"Real-money purchase"}]}

details.explanation: The player commits time to learning, combat, rescue and logistics. This is the starting player input; the downstream account balance is an in-game resource, not a substitute for time.
details.implications: Reward design allocates player attention between fighting and support roles.
details.prompt: Which useful role makes the best use of a new player’s time?
details.reviewFingerprint: {"label":"Spend Time","kind":"initial_sink_node","inputRole":"time","sources":[],"sinks":["Player time"],"values":[],"notes":"Play, learn and contribute to the team.","edges":[{"from":"time","to":"cash","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"Beginning / continuing a player journey"}]}

details.explanation: Real-world spending buys game access and optional Supporter cosmetics. The developer policy says cash and gold are not sold.
details.implications: Keep commercial revenue separate from earned currency and player-to-player transfers.
details.prompt: Can cosmetic purchases support development without distorting role affordability?
details.reviewFingerprint: {"label":"Spend Money","kind":"initial_sink_node","inputRole":"money","sources":[],"sinks":["Real money"],"values":[],"notes":"Game access and optional cosmetics; no cash purchase.","edges":[{"from":"money","to":"commerce","type":"normal","feedback":false,"label":"Real-money purchase"}]}

details.explanation: Keeping a usable balance and funding team infrastructure can preserve a choice of useful roles. This is an analytical outcome of the researched mechanics, not a guaranteed victory or measured return.
details.implications: A healthy economy makes contribution sustainable while still rewarding successful play.
details.prompt: Can poorer players contribute meaningfully alongside wealthy specialists?

details.explanation: Optional cosmetic entitlements provide an expression outcome for real-money spending. They are not depicted as a source of account cash.
details.implications: The commercial path terminates in access and identity rather than purchased economic power.
details.prompt: Are the Supporter extras compelling without providing a cash advantage?
